name: Illyrian Pantheon
note: Hub collective for the deities of the western-Balkan Illyrian peoples, attested chiefly through Latin votive inscriptions of the Roman period.

name: Medaurus
note: Great rider-god and tutelary deity of Risinium (Risan), depicted as a mounted lancer; attested in inscriptions and a dedication from Lambaesis honoring the god of Risinium.

name: Redon
note: Tutelary sea and travel god of Lissus (Lezhe); attested on coins of Lissus and votive inscriptions, also found at Santa Maria di Leuca.

name: Bindus
note: Water-god of the Iapodes, worshipped at the spring of Privilica near Bihac; attested in Latin inscriptions as Bindus Neptunus, equated with Neptune.

name: Tadenus
note: Local Dalmatian deity attested by inscriptions near the source of the Bosna river; sometimes associated with Apollo, of uncertain function (likely healing/spring).

name: Vidasus
note: Illyrian forest/woodland god attested at Topusko in Pannonia, regularly paired with the goddess Thana and identified with the Roman Silvanus.

name: Thana
note: Illyrian goddess of the hunt and woodland, consort of Vidasus at Topusko, identified with the Roman Diana.

name: Eia
note: Illyrian goddess attested in inscriptions of the Histrian/north-Adriatic region (e.g. at Nesactium and Pola); function uncertain, likely a local tutelary/protective goddess.

name: En (Enji)
note: Reconstructed Illyrian fire-god proposed as the source of the Albanian weekday e enjte (Thursday); inferred from linguistic/comparative evidence rather than direct inscription.

name: Dei-Paturos
note: Illyrian-Thracian sky/father deity (name cognate with Indo-European *Dyeus-pater), attested for the Bessoi/Thracian-Illyrian borderlands; sometimes counted among Illyrian deities.

name: Sentona
note: Illyrian (Liburnian/Histrian) goddess attested in votive inscriptions of the north-eastern Adriatic, possibly a goddess of travel/health; often paired in cult with Eia.

name: Anzotica
note: Liburnian goddess worshipped at Aenona (Nin), identified with Venus in local inscriptions and statuary.
